items.english: And he, growing drowsy, showed no sign of readily withdrawing to his own room. The room Taki had fixed upon as his study had, for some reason, never been wired for electric light. An extension left half begun and abandoned these four or five years, it had, one gathered, been meant perhaps for an altar room. To recover his long reversed day and night, he had rather welcomed this and had left unlit there alone the light that could easily have been drawn in. And only in the daytime, and then very rarely, for he was unused to it, on cloudy days when he could not go to the sea, did he sit at his desk. When night came on, half out of eccentricity, he would read by the light of an oil lamp or a candlestand, or give himself to musings truly foolish as a 'snowscape.'
notes: 'Altar room' renders what the bible takes to be a Buddhist altar room extension; the passage only conjectures its purpose. 'Snowscape' kept hard to hold the concordance with p58 and p160.
Speaker unstated; taken as the wife from the exchange that follows.

items.english: "It has grown dark, so walk me as far as town while you see me off. For once I want to eat somewhere else. And I have a little money on me today."

Hearing that, Taki agreed on the spot. His wife, with the revelry next door growing livelier by the minute, all for trying other means next carp day and making a quick catch before the water clouded, for taking the long view —
notes: Second sentence left incomplete as in the Japanese, closing with the dash where p81 and p82 break in as the voices from the next room. 'Catch' kept for the concordance.

items.english: "Once it is clouded, it is more than our hands can manage, whatever you say! Ha ha ha..."
notes: Speaker left floating between A and B as in the Japanese; rough workmen's speech kept plain, without borrowed dialect. 'Clouded' kept for the clouding water concordance.

items.english: "It truly nettles me, I cannot bear it. Come to this, it is pride. I cannot wait patiently for the water to clear."
notes: Speaker left floating as in the Japanese. 'Clear' kept against 'clouded' in p81.

data.say: Drafted the drowsy study passage and the turn toward town with workmen's voices breaking in.
